'''Jenny Yue-fon Yang''' ({{lang-zh|t=楊又芳|p=Yáng Yòufāng}})<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=http://dailynews.sina.com/bg/news/usa/usnews/chinesedaily/20170113/10027691990.html|title=台裔學者獲美工程師最高榮譽|last=楊|first=婷專|date=January 13, 2017|website=Sina Daily News|publisher=[[Sina Corp]]|language=zh|access-date=2018-11-30}}</ref> is an American chemist. She is a professor of chemistry at the [[University of California, Irvine]], where she leads a research group focused on inorganic chemistry, catalysis, and solar fuels.

== Early life and education ==
Jenny Yue-fon Yang<ref name=":3">{{Cite thesis|last=Yang|first=Jenny Yue-fon|date=2007|title=Distal hydrogen-bonding effects and cofacial bimetallic salen architectures for oxygen activation chemistry|publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology|hdl=1721.1/40873|type=Thesis }}</ref> was born to a [[Taiwanese American]] family in the [[San Fernando Valley]] and raised in [[Chatsworth, Los Angeles]]. Her parents were Taiwanese immigrants.<ref name=":5" />

Yang studied chemistry at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where she worked in the laboratory of [[Jeffrey R. Long]]. Yang synthesized novel [[Prussian blue]] analog materials and analyzed their magnetic properties.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yang|first1=Jenny Y.|last2=Shores|first2=Matthew P.|last3=Sokol|first3=Jennifer J.|last4=Long|first4=Jeffrey R.|date=2003-03-01|title=High-Nuclearity Metal−Cyanide Clusters: Synthesis, Magnetic Properties, and Inclusion Behavior of Open-Cage Species Incorporating [(tach)M(CN)3] (M = Cr, Fe, Co) Complexes|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ic026065f|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=42|issue=5|pages=1403–1419|doi=10.1021/ic026065f|pmid=12611505 |issn=0020-1669|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She graduated in 2001 with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in chemistry, and moved to the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] for graduate studies in the laboratory of [[Daniel G. Nocera]]. Yang's work in the Nocera lab focused on the synthesis of novel [[Salen ligand|salen]] complexes that mimic the activity of the [[catalase]] enzyme, and exhibit [[epoxidation]] activity towards [[olefins]].<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2008-08-04|title=Manganese amido-imine bisphenol Hangman complexes|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S004040390800899X|journal=Tetrahedron Letters|language=en|volume=49|issue=32|pages=4796–4798|doi=10.1016/j.tetlet.2008.05.111|issn=0040-4039|last1=Yang |first1=Jenny Y. |last2=Nocera |first2=Daniel G. |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yang|first1=Jenny Y.|last2=Nocera|first2=Daniel G.|date=2007-07-01|title=Catalase and Epoxidation Activity of Manganese Salen Complexes Bearing Two Xanthene Scaffolds|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja070358w|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=129|issue=26|pages=8192–8198|doi=10.1021/ja070358w|pmid=17552520 |bibcode=2007JAChS.129.8192Y |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> She graduated with her Ph.D. in 2007.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Directory {{!}} UCI Department of Chemistry|url=http://www.chem.uci.edu/people/jenny-y-yangv|access-date=2018-10-29|website=www.chem.uci.edu|language=en}}{{Dead link|date=March 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

== Career ==
Yang moved to Washington to conduct postdoctoral research at the [[Pacific Northwest National Laboratory|Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL)]], where she worked with Daniel L. DuBois on mechanistic studies of H<sub>2</sub> oxidation with nickel bis([[Diphosphines|diphosphine]]) complexes.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yang|first1=Jenny Y.|last2=Bullock|first2=R. Morris|last3=Shaw|first3=Wendy J.|last4=Twamley|first4=Brendan|last5=Fraze|first5=Kendra|last6=DuBois|first6=M. Rakowski|last7=DuBois|first7=Daniel L.|date=2009-04-29|title=Mechanistic Insights into Catalytic H2 Oxidation by Ni Complexes Containing a Diphosphine Ligand with a Positioned Amine Base|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja900483x|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=131|issue=16|pages=5935–5945|doi=10.1021/ja900483x|pmid=19341269 |bibcode=2009JAChS.131.5935Y |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yang|first1=Jenny Y.|last2=Chen|first2=Shentan|last3=Dougherty|first3=William G.|last4=Kassel|first4=W. Rakowski|date=2010-11-09|title=Hydrogen oxidation catalysis by a nickel diphosphine complex with pendant tert-butyl amines|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2010/cc/c0cc03246h|journal=Chemical Communications|language=en|volume=46|issue=45|pages=8618–8620|doi=10.1039/C0CC03246H|pmid=20938535 |issn=1364-548X|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yang|first1=Jenny Y.|last2=Smith|first2=Stuart E.|last3=Liu|first3=Tianbiao|last4=Dougherty|first4=William G.|last5=Hoffert|first5=Wesley A.|last6=Kassel|first6=W. Morris|date=2013-07-03|title=Two Pathways for Electrocatalytic Oxidation of Hydrogen by a Nickel Bis(diphosphine) Complex with Pendant Amines in the Second Coordination Sphere|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja400705a|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=135|issue=26|pages=9700–9712|doi=10.1021/ja400705a|pmid=23631473 |bibcode=2013JAChS.135.9700Y |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 2009, she was hired as a senior staff scientist at PNNL. She then worked as a research scientist at the Molecular Catalysis group of the [[Joint Center for Artificial Photosynthesis]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]]. In 2013, Yang joined the faculty at [[University of California, Irvine]] as an assistant professor of chemistry.

== Awards and honors ==
Yang has received several awards. These include the [[Department of Energy (United States)|DoE]] Early Career Research Award in 2014<ref name=":5" /> and the [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|National Science Foundation CAREER Award]] in 2016. In 2017, she was honored with the [[Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers]] (PECASE), the Kavli Frontiers of Science Fellowship, and a [[Research Corporation]] Advanced Energy Materials Scialog Fellowship.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=UC Irvine - Faculty Profile System|url=http://www.faculty.uci.edu/profile.cfm?faculty_id=5967|access-date=2018-10-29|website=www.faculty.uci.edu|language=en}}</ref> In 2018, she was awarded a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]], and in 2019 she was named a [[Camille Dreyfus Teacher-Scholar Awards|Camille Dreyfus Teacher-Scholar]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-05-02|title=2019 Camille Dreyfus Teacher-Scholar Awards|url=https://www.dreyfus.org/2019-camille-dreyfus-teacher-scholar-awards/|access-date=2021-06-10|website=Dreyfus Foundation|language=en-US |author1=Moderator }}</ref> In 2015, Yang was selected as a member of the [[Global Young Academy]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jenny Yang|url=https://globalyoungacademy.net/jenny-y/|access-date=2021-06-10|website=Global Young Academy|language=en-US}}</ref> and in 2018, she was named a [[CIFAR]] Azrieli Global Scholars.<ref>{{Cite web|date=September 6, 2018|title=Announcing the 2018 Class of CIFAR Azrieli Global Scholars|url=https://www.cifar.ca/cifarnews/2018/09/06/announcing-the-2018-class-of-cifar-azrieli-global-scholars|access-date=2018-11-29|website=CIFAR|language=en}}</ref>
